title: Finite diagonal totals for the bounded-minus resolution bicomplex
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $C$ be a preadditive category with a zero object and finite coproducts, and let $\iota:C\to A$ be fully faithful and additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. Let $\Lambda$ be a left-resolution datum [lem-sfb-left-resolution-reduced-api] for $\iota$ whose functor preserves zero morphisms, and let $K$ be an integer cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] in $A$ with $K^p=0$ for all $p>b$. Form $B_K$ as the $\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z$ bicomplex whose $(p,q)$-term is the $q$-th term of the cochain-complex resolution $R(K^p)$ of [lem-sfb-left-resolution-objectwise-cochain], with differentials induced by the two complex directions; its total is formed from the diagonal coproducts. Then $B_K$ and its termwise image under $\iota$ are zero in every bidegree with resolution degree $q>0$ and in every first degree $p>b$. Consequently both bicomplexes have total complexes for the shape $\operatorname{up}(\mathbb Z)$.

proof.text: Use the objectwise resolution functor $R$ and its induced maps to form $B_K$ by applying the homological-complex map in the complex degree: its $(p,q)$-term is $R(K^p)^q$, and applying $\iota$ termwise gives the mapped bicomplex. The two differentials are the complex differential of $K$ and the resolution differential, with the standard commuting-bicomplex signs.

The objectwise resolution is strictly supported in cochain degrees $q\le 0$, and the same is true after applying $\iota$. Therefore $B_K^{p,q}$ and $(\iota B_K)^{p,q}$ are zero whenever $q>0$, for every $p$.

source.place: support instances for the cochain resolution and its mapped image, lines 52–64

proof.text: If $p>b$, then $K^p$ is a zero object, so $\mathrm{id}_{K^p}=0_{K^p,K^p}$. By the recursion in [lem-sfb-left-resolution-objectwise-cochain], $R(X)^{-n}$ is, for $n\ge0$, exactly the $n$-th term of the $\mathbb N$-indexed chain complex $\Lambda.\mathrm{chainComplex}(X)$ (degree $0$: $F(X)$; degree $1$: $F(\ker\pi_X)$; degree $n+2$: $F(\ker\iota(d))$), $R(X)^q=0$ for $q>0$, and $R(f)$ has components $\Lambda.\mathrm{chainComplexMap}(f)$ in degrees $\le0$. Functoriality of $R$ gives $R(\mathrm{id}_{K^p})=\mathrm{id}_{R(K^p)}$, and the zero-morphism equation [lem-sfb-left-resolution-chain-complex-map-zero] (using that $F$ preserves zero morphisms) gives $R(0)=0$ in every degree $\le0$, while the degrees $q>0$ are zero objects anyway. Hence the identity of every term $R(K^p)^q$ is zero, so every term is a zero object of $C$. An additive functor sends zero objects to zero objects, so every $\iota(R(K^p)^q)$ is zero as well. Hence both $B_K^{p,q}$ and $(\iota B_K)^{p,q}$ are zero for every $p>b$ and every $q$.

Apply the bounded-support totalization statement [lem-sfb-left-resolution-additive-total-transport] to $B_K$ with $F=\iota$ and $D=A$. Its hypotheses hold because $C$ has a zero object and finite coproducts, $A$ is preadditive as part of being abelian, and $\iota$ is additive. The support established in the preceding two steps is exactly the condition that terms vanish for $p>b$ or $q>0$. The theorem therefore supplies the diagonal total complexes for both $B_K$ and its termwise image under $\iota$, with shape $\operatorname{up}(\mathbb Z)$.
